senses.definition: (anatomy) A large organ in the body that stores and metabolizes nutrients, destroys toxins and produces bile. It is responsible for thousands of biochemical reactions.
examples: Steve Jobs is a famous liver transplant recipient.

senses.definition: (countable, uncountable) This organ, as taken from animals used as food.
examples: I'd like some goose liver pate.
You could fry up some chicken livers for a tasty treat. — Nah, I don't like chicken liver.

quotes.text: "I should think you've rocked the boat enough already by refusing to eat liver."

senses.definition: A dark brown colour, tinted with red and gray, like the colour of liver.
(obsolete chemistry) Any of various chemical compounds—particularly sulfides—thought to resemble livers in color.
examples: He gave his horse some liver of antimony.

senses.definition: Of the colour of liver (dark brown, tinted with red and gray).

quotes.text: His friend Rothwell, who had the use of the best Laveracks for breeding purposes, wrote him that one of his puppies was liver and white.

examples: Thou king of heaven, which […] Dost see the secret of each livers heart.

quotes.text: When as the wandring Scots and Picthts King Marius had subdude, He gave the Liuers dwellings.

quotes.text: They must instantly have been detected by the present Livers that were upon the place.
